Seems like this has a lot of promise, if only there were people playing it. 

Performs terribly in the actual rounds for some reason, even on "Max FPS" setting, which is really strange.

This game is so busted bro spent 10 mins in matchmaking only for it to crash once a game was found

Edit: Found a game, stuttering was so intense and GPU artifacting began. Had to close the game asap before my ♥♥♥♥ melted. Mind you this game released a year before my GPU.

# Overall game feel
The game feels like MW reboot era Ground War but free. The vehicles handle like Battlefield 4 more, which is a plus. Movement is much clunkier. Gunplay is like MW reboot era to a t, down to having armor that needs breaking.

# Quality of Life
The game is Euro-jank, plain and simple. The quality of life is something you would expect from late 2000s/early 2010s shooters, arguably worse since even the likes of Black Ops 2 had better QoL. For example, you can't even change the mouse sensitivity properly without going into config files.

# Optimization and servers
Really bad. Can't even maintain 60fps. The low playerbase means that Asian players get really bad ping. Still much better than the state it was even 2 years ago though. Euro players can definitely hop in matches quickly nowadays.

# Would I recommend?
Only hesitantly. If the idea of a euro-jank ground war competitor appeals to you, then you would love this game. It's no Battlefield, mind you.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe extremely long matchmaking times and broken party systems that prevent joining games or playing with friends.

citations.review_text: bro so bad first if i join a game it takes 1 billion years just make some solo or battle royale just a ripoff of battlefield 6

Mixed Review

I rarely leave negative reviews, especially for games I actually want to like, but World War 3 is simply not ready for live service yet.

The only reason I downloaded this game was to play with a friend. Instead, when joining a party, I constantly get the error “not connected to player service.” This alone killed the experience before it even started.

For context, I play a lot of games   Marvel Rivals, Overwatch, Counter-Strike, Enshrouded, Valheim, and many others   and I never run into issues like this. This game, unfortunately, takes the cake.

I tried Googling fixes and was shocked at how much work it expects you to do just to play. After seeing that, it honestly turned me off, which is why my playtime is so low.

I did manage to play two matches, and here’s my honest take:

Good

Gunplay is good

Graphics look good

Gun customization is great

Bad

Lobbies had a lot of bots (at least in my experience)

Party system is broken, which defeats the whole point of playing with friends

Overall, I don’t have much more to say based on the limited time I was able to play. I left this review specifically because of the party service issue. Until that’s fixed, I can’t recommend it.

OVER AND OUT!

I lost access to my old account and only recently returned to the game. I was thrown into matches with bots, which allowed me to level up my new account at least a little right from the start. Good idea. Finding matches still takes a very long time. The new map kicks me out at the start, I barely managed to get through. Overall, it's clear that work is being done on the project, so my feedback is more positive; I still like this shooter. I wish the developers would focus on fixing bugs because I enjoy the game, but the inability to get into matches honestly kills my desire to keep trying.

I don't love making this review, because there was a window there in 2022 and 2023 where I absolutely loved this game. WW3 was one of those projects with a good core gameplay loop but was always let down by something else: too little content, too few updates, poor server performance, a crappy launcher, too much focus on microtransactions when still trying to establish a player base, and other overall mismanagement issues.

In 2025, what we have is a game without a player base. New ownership has picked up the game and is delivering updates, but at this point it is a drip-feed of tweaks and additions being handed to a player base that doesn't exist. The game has averaged fewer than 200 players since January 2024, and that has now dropped to fewer than 100 players. Trying to play this game is often an exercise of ending up in a waiting room with 3 other players, and watching people join and quit one-by-one.

The positives for the game are still there. The gameplay is a more hardcore Battlefield style experience. Weapon recoil is stronger than Battlefield's often laser-y guns. Movement is weightier and should appeal to players who think BF is drifting too close to COD-style movement. Weapon customization is also a major strong point of the game, and an area where the project punches way above its weight.

This game has had multiple soft-relaunches since its disastrous original 2018 early access release. It's going to take something big and attention-grabbing to get people to come back and try the game again, especially players jaded from the previous short lived re-launches.

citations.review_text: World War 3 has a solid foundation, but it still feels like a game that hasn’t quite figured out what it wants to be. The gunplay is decent, customization is deep, and the modern military setting has a lot of potential. When everything works, matches can actually be pretty fun and tense. Unfortunately, consistency is the biggest issue. Player population can be hit or miss, which leads to uneven matchmaking and repetitive encounters. Progression feels slow and sometimes unrewarding, and there are moments where it feels like you’re grinding more than actually enjoying the gameplay. Performance and stability have improved compared to earlier versions, but bugs and jank still pop up often enough to be noticeable. The tactical elements and large scale battles are interesting on paper, but they don’t always come together in practice. Maps can feel underutilized, and teamwork isn’t always encouraged as much as it should be for a game that clearly wants to be tactical rather than arcadey.

In 2025, what we have is a game without a player base. World War 3 – From Promising Tactical Shooter to a Corporate Disaster

I was genuinely excited for World War 3 when it first gained traction. Youtubers praised its tactical gameplay, deep customization, solid gunplay, great maps, and vehicle integration. And you know what? They were right — at the time. It had serious potential to be something special.

But fast-forward to today and it's turned into a flaming mess of disappointment.

Paid cosmetics shoved in your face, non-stop — the kind that make it painfully obvious this game was twisted into a cash grab. When the player count started tanking, the devs pivoted to free-to-play, clearly in a desperate attempt to revive interest. It didn’t fix anything.

The updates are lazy, the servers are garbage, and for some reason we’re forced into using a separate launcher, as if that makes anything better. Still no custom server browser, still no server region selection — in a multiplayer shooter? Seriously?

Worse yet, the developers’ communication is borderline insulting. When people leave detailed, passionate feedback, they respond with short, off-topic PR nonsense that dodges the real problems. Are you even reading the community posts? We’re literally trying to help make the game better. Why are you not listening?

Here’s a question you won’t answer:
Are your executives or shareholders holding you hostage? Is that why every design choice screams "maximize profit, screw the players"?

This game went from being a rare gem with a future to yet another soulless shell pumped full of monetization and mismanagement. It hurts more because it was good.

If you’re reading this and considering playing WW3 — don’t. At least not until the devs grow a spine and start listening to the people who actually care about the game more than the damn cash shop.

I'm quitting this game now. IT'S UNPLAYABLE.

There are many problems with this game.
First, there is a bad team balance system. The balance is too serious because one team only puts in those who are good at it, and the other team only puts in those who are bad at it. As a result, teams that are good at it are boring and not fun, and those who are bad are annoyed and not fun.
Second, the respawn bug is not correct. If you are unlucky to respond to a squad member, you will get stuck in the object. Because of this, people who are stuck can't even leave, but this isn't a big problem. A serious problem is that people who are stuck can attack enemies outside the object, but people who are outside the object can't. A more serious problem is that when such a bug occurs in or near a base, the opposing team has no choice but to abandon the base.
Third, Wallhack and ESP play the game. People who use the cheat program frequently change their nicknames, ruining the game, but the management takes no action.
Fourth, there is no Asian server. Those who do Asian servers because they don't have Asian servers are at a disadvantage, and even if they do well, they suspect that they used the Hack program.

The game is a mixed bag.

Initially, it felt good to play something similar to BF3. You learn new maps, tactics, you mod your weapon etc. Though, after reaching the final level 51, having most weapon and their customizations unlocked, the game feels more and more repetetive, even boring.

Weapons feel the same after a while, even when customized. I would prefer more unique feeling per weapon and a wider variety of assault rifles, SMGs etc. Familiar ones from other games are missing (licensing?). Game modes do not very much: the most popular ones remain "capture the flag" and TDM.

Things that are annoying / can be improved:

- weaponized drones and helicopters are overpowered. anti-air missiles are heavy equipment, crippling movement in the game just to counter air vehicles
- more powerful RPGs such as Panzerfaust take ages to be unlocked. Regular RPGs are like throwing stones at a tank
- when lying down on you back you sometimes get stuck in a position unable to move or get back up again
- as mentioned before, game modes and weapons / custmizations do not feel "unique"
- sometimes the game is lagging even with good ping

All in all a game with good graphics and gameplay, with a some rough edges remaining. The game has potential but lacks content to keep me interested in the long run.


Ideas:

- add knives for close quarter combat. In BF3 you could mock your opponent in an inattentive moment (in a positive way)
- add new game modes for existing maps: 
   - gun master (level up weapons as fast as possible via kills, starting with a knive -> handgun -> SMG -> assault rifle -> MG -> sniper rifle)

Game is Dead

-bugs bugs bugs (people in walls, spawning issues and etc)
-playerbase is dead = You can't unlock the good weapons, you'd have to get kills on certain maps to unlock them. But there are no games on those maps anymore due to the small player base. You can only play tactical ops over and over again against the same (sweaty/cheating) opponents.

I'm quitting this game now. IT'S UNPLAYABLE.

overall a great game and more fun than COD or battlefield in a modern conflict, essentially being a mix of the two with realistic combat but killstreaks.
HOWEVER, the game is VERY dead. I can NOT find ANY server on team deathmatch or domination which some maps are limited to, thus limiting the ability to actually unlock some of the items you want for free.

With the game being free to play I can't not recommend giving it a go. Low population might mean difficulties finding a game from time to time but most of the time there is more than enough players online for a few matches to be going with room for more to join. It plays like a blend of battlefield 3/4 and older call of duty games with scorestreaks being the way of bringing in your own kitted out vehicles. This helps ensure that there isn't necessarily always a vehicle shwacking your guys. There is also the ability to equip whatever weapons you want as your primary and secondary weapons. This is offset by a weight system and additionally allowing different levels of armor, again offset by weight. What sets this game apart in my opinion is this system and it makes for interesting build choices. You could run an LMG and an SMG as backup, but that's gonna be pretty heavy on its own with all that ammo, do you skimp on armor to keep a reasonable load or do you take a reasonable amount and be at maximum load? choices choices.

claims.claim: Matches suffer from team imbalance issues where skilled players are grouped together on one side.

citations.review_text:
The audio got a ringing sound which is annoying. There is no balanced system which can lead to one sided matches. The vehicles are OP NERF THEM. NERF UAV TOO NEEDS LONGER COOLDOWNS. 

The launcher sucks and download speed is super slow. Game is dead

There are many problems with this game.
First, there is a bad team balance system. The balance is too serious because one team only puts in those who are good at it, and the other team only puts in those who are bad at it. As a result, teams that are good at it are boring and not fun, and those who are bad are annoyed and not fun.
Second, the respawn bug is not correct. If you are unlucky to respond to a squad member, you will get stuck in the object. Because of this, people who are stuck can't even leave, but this isn't a big problem. A serious problem is that people who are stuck can attack enemies outside the object, but people who are outside the object can't. A more serious problem is that when such a bug occurs in or near a base, the opposing team has no choice but to abandon the base.
Third, Wallhack and ESP play the game. People who use the cheat program frequently change their nicknames, ruining the game, but the management takes no action.
Fourth, there is no Asian server. Those who do Asian servers because they don't have Asian servers are at a disadvantage, and even if they do well, they suspect that they used the Hack program.
